# Tellers OTIO timeline reference

A tellers timeline is an [OpenTimelineIO](https://opentimelineio.readthedocs.io) JSON document with extra data under `metadata["tellers.ai"]` and in tellers effects. New to the format? Start with the [reading guide](reading-otio.md).

- [Objects](#objects)
- [Tellers effects](#tellers-effects)

## Objects

### Timeline

The document. Its `tracks` stack holds every track; timeline-wide settings (fonts, text styles) live in its `metadata["tellers.ai"]`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Timeline.1"` | Always `Timeline.1`. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.availableFonts` lists the fonts text clips may use, `tellers.ai.textStyles` the shared CSS classes of rich-text clips. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `tracks` | [Stack](#stack) |  |  | The stack of every track. |

### Stack

The tracks of the timeline, composited together. Tracks render in list order: the first is the bottom layer, the last the top one (painter's order). Its `effects` apply to the whole composited image.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Stack.1"` | Always `Stack.1`. |
| `children` | array of [Track](#track) |  |  | The tracks, bottom layer first. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied over the whole composited image (the timeline stage). |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Timeline markers, in timeline time. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |

### Track

A row of items played one after the other: each item starts where the previous one ends, so a track's timing is the sum of its items' durations. Video tracks carry picture only and audio tracks sound only.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Track.1"` | Always `Track.1`. |
| `children` | array of [Item](#item) |  |  | The items, in play order. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied to each clip of the track (the track stage). |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` | A disabled track is neither drawn nor heard. |
| `kind` | [TrackKind](#trackkind) | yes |  | `video`, `audio` or `other`. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Track markers, in timeline time. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the track id; `tellers.ai.created_by: "auto"` marks tracks the library created; `tellers.ai.textStyles` overrides the timeline's. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name, e.g. `V1` or `A2`. |

### TrackKind

What a track carries. Read case-insensitively (`Video` and `video` both parse); written lowercase.

Values: `"video"` \| `"audio"` \| `"other"`.

### Item

An entry of a track: a clip, or a gap of empty time.

One of [Clip](#clip), [Gap](#gap).

### Clip

A piece of media (or generated content) placed on a track for the duration of its `source_range`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Clip.2"` | `Clip.2` (`Clip.1` is read too). |
| `active_media_reference_key` | string \| null |  |  | Which `media_references` entry plays; `DEFAULT_MEDIA` when unset. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied to this clip only (the clip stage), in order. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` | A disabled clip is neither drawn nor heard; it still takes its time. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Clip markers, in source (media) time. |
| `media_references` | map of string → [MediaReference](#mediareference) |  |  | The clip's media, by key; usually a single `DEFAULT_MEDIA`. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the item id, `tellers.ai.group_id` links clips that move together, and the Resolve `Link Group ID` ties a video to its audio (sync partners). |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `source_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) | yes |  | The part of the media played: `start_time` in the media's own time, and `duration`, which is also how long the clip lasts on the track. |

### Gap

Empty time on a track: nothing is drawn or heard for its duration.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Gap.1"` | `Gap.1`. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Kept for OTIO round trips; nothing applies them. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Kept for OTIO round trips; the API places no markers on gaps. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the item id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `source_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) | yes |  | Only `duration` matters: how long the gap lasts. |

### MediaReference

What a clip plays, chosen by `OTIO_SCHEMA`. `MissingReference.1` is also accepted and read as an external reference with an empty `target_url`.

#### `ExternalReference.1`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | `"ExternalReference.1"` | yes |  | Picks the kind of reference. |
| `available_image_bounds` | any JSON |  |  | OTIO image bounds; unused by the player. |
| `available_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) \| null |  |  | The time range the media file covers, in its own time; `source_range` stays inside it. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai` holds asset details such as the asset id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `target_url` | string |  | `""` | URL of the media file. Resolved from the asset before playback and stripped before saving, so a stored timeline may have it empty. |

#### `GeneratorReference.1`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | `"GeneratorReference.1"` | yes |  | Picks the kind of reference. |
| `available_image_bounds` | any JSON |  |  | OTIO image bounds; unused by the player. |
| `available_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) \| null |  |  | The time range the media file covers, in its own time; `source_range` stays inside it. |
| `generator_kind` | string | yes |  | `Rich` (Resolve Rich Text: HTML), `Text` (plain text), `Shape` (rectangle, ellipse, line) or another generator. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai` holds asset details such as the asset id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `parameters` | [GeneratorParameters](#generatorparameters) |  |  | The generator's parameters; see GeneratorParameters. |

### GeneratorParameters

The parameters of a generator reference: a Resolve `Rich Text` block for `generator_kind: "Rich"`, or the player's own keys for `Text` and `Shape` generators (see the reading guide). Other keys are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Resolve_OTIO` | array of [ResolveOTIOEffect](#resolveotioeffect) \| null |  |  | Resolve effects of the generator: for Rich Text, a `Rich Text` effect with the `title blob` HTML, `position`, zoom and rotation. |

### Effect

An effect on a clip, a track or the stack. Tellers effects are named `tellers.ai.<Effect>` and keep their parameters in `metadata["tellers.ai"].parameters` (see [Tellers effects](#tellers-effects)); Resolve transforms, volume and crop are `Resolve Effect`s with a `Resolve_OTIO` block. Other OTIO keys (e.g. `time_scalar`) are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Effect.1"` | `Effect.1`; OTIO's `LinearTimeWarp.1` and `FreezeFrame.1` are read too. |
| `effect_name` | string |  | `""` | Which effect: `tellers.ai.<Effect>` for tellers effects, `Resolve Effect` for Resolve ones. |
| `enabled` | boolean \| null |  |  | `false` turns the effect off without removing it; absent means enabled. |
| `metadata` | [EffectMetadata](#effectmetadata) |  |  | Where the effect's settings live; see EffectMetadata. |
| `name` | string |  | `""` | Display label. |

### EffectMetadata

The metadata of an effect. Keys other than `Resolve_OTIO` (notably `tellers.ai`) are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Resolve_OTIO` | [ResolveOTIOEffect](#resolveotioeffect) \| null |  |  | The Resolve effect of a `Resolve Effect` (Transform, volume, Cropping). |

### Marker

A note on a point or range of the edit. `marked_range` is in the time of the object holding it: timeline time on the stack and tracks, source (media) time on a clip.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Marker.2"` | `Marker.2`. |
| `color` | string |  | `"RED"` | An OTIO marker color (`RED`, `GREEN`, `BLUE`, ...). |
| `comment` | string |  | `""` | Body of the note. |
| `marked_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) |  |  | The flagged point (zero duration) or range. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the marker id, `tellers.ai.created_by` its author. |
| `name` | string |  | `""` | Title of the note. |

### TimeRange

A span of time: `start_time` and `duration`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"TimeRange.1"` | `TimeRange.1`. |
| `duration` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) | yes |  | How long it lasts. |
| `start_time` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) | yes |  | Where the range starts. |

### RationalTime

A time as `value / rate` seconds (e.g. `{ value: 48, rate: 24 }` is 2 s).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"RationalTime.1"` | `RationalTime.1`. |
| `rate` | number | yes |  | Units per second, e.g. a frame rate (`1` for plain seconds). |
| `value` | number | yes |  | Number of `1 / rate` units. |

### ResolveOTIOEffect

A DaVinci Resolve effect, as Resolve's OTIO export writes it: in an `Effect`'s `metadata.Resolve_OTIO`, or in a generator's `parameters.Resolve_OTIO` list.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Effect Name` | string | yes |  | Resolve's name for the effect, e.g. `Transform` or `Rich Text`. |
| `Enabled` | boolean |  | `false` | Whether Resolve applies it. |
| `Name` | string |  | `""` | Display name. |
| `Parameters` | array of [ResolveOTIOParameter](#resolveotioparameter) |  |  | The effect's parameters. |
| `Type` | number |  | `0` | Resolve's numeric effect type (e.g. `2` Transform, `24` Rich Text). |

## Tellers effects

Every effect the player renders has the same shape: an `Effect.1` whose `effect_name` is `tellers.ai.<Effect>` and whose parameters are in `metadata["tellers.ai"].parameters`. A bare `<Effect>` name (written before the prefix) is still read. Unknown names are ignored, and an effect with `"enabled": false` is skipped.

```json
{
  "OTIO_SCHEMA": "Effect.1",
  "effect_name": "tellers.ai.Blur",
  "metadata": { "tellers.ai": { "parameters": { "strength": 6 } } }
}
```

The same effect can sit on a clip, a track (applied to each of its clips) or the stack (applied over the whole image); clip effects apply first, then the track's, then the timeline's. Where an effect applies once (`Transform`, `Blend`, `Volume`, ...), the first enabled one wins. Parameters left out take the player's defaults.

| Effect | `effect_name` | Applies to | Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Blur](#effect-blur) | `tellers.ai.Blur` | video (picture) | `strength`, `quality` |
| [Pixelate](#effect-pixelate) | `tellers.ai.Pixelate` | video (picture) | `size` |
| [Adjustment](#effect-adjustment) | `tellers.ai.Adjustment` | video (picture) | `gamma`, `saturation`, `contrast`, `brightness`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha` |
| [ColorMatrix](#effect-colormatrix) | `tellers.ai.ColorMatrix` | video (picture) | `preset`, `hue`, `amount` |
| [HslAdjustment](#effect-hsladjustment) | `tellers.ai.HslAdjustment` | video (picture) | `hue`, `saturation`, `lightness`, `colorize`, `amount` |
| [Noise](#effect-noise) | `tellers.ai.Noise` | video (picture) | `amount`, `speed`, `seed` |
| [RGBSplit](#effect-rgbsplit) | `tellers.ai.RGBSplit` | video (picture) | `amount`, `angle` |
| [ZoomBlur](#effect-zoomblur) | `tellers.ai.ZoomBlur` | video (picture) | `strength`, `centerX`, `centerY`, `innerRadius` |
| [DropShadow](#effect-dropshadow) | `tellers.ai.DropShadow` | video (picture) | `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `blur`, `alpha`, `color` |
| [ChromaKey](#effect-chromakey) | `tellers.ai.ChromaKey` | video (picture) | `color`, `similarity`, `smoothness`, `spill`, `choke` |
| [Border](#effect-border) | `tellers.ai.Border` | video (picture) | `width`, `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, `opacity`, `color` |
| [MotionBlur](#effect-motionblur) | `tellers.ai.MotionBlur` | video (picture) | `shutterAngle`, `shutterPhase`, `samples` |
| [Transform](#effect-transform) | `tellers.ai.Transform` | video (picture) | `x`, `y`, `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `rotation`, `opacity` |
| [Blend](#effect-blend) | `tellers.ai.Blend` | video (picture) | `mode` |
| [Mask](#effect-mask) | `tellers.ai.Mask` | video (picture) | `shape`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `rotation`, `corner_radius`, `feather`, `opacity`, `invert`, `mode`, `closed`, `points` |
| [TrackMatte](#effect-trackmatte) | `tellers.ai.TrackMatte` | video (picture) | `mode`, `track` |
| [Volume](#effect-volume) | `tellers.ai.Volume` | audio (sound) | `volume`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut` |
| [Pan](#effect-pan) | `tellers.ai.Pan` | audio (sound) | `pan` |
| [TimeWarp](#effect-timewarp) | `tellers.ai.TimeWarp` | playback speed | `speed`, `preserve_pitch` |
| [TextTypewriter](#effect-texttypewriter) | `tellers.ai.TextTypewriter` | text clips | `progress` |
| [TextWordReveal](#effect-textwordreveal) | `tellers.ai.TextWordReveal` | text clips | `progress`, `style` |
| [TextKaraoke](#effect-textkaraoke) | `tellers.ai.TextKaraoke` | text clips | `progress`, `scale`, `color` |
| [TextWave](#effect-textwave) | `tellers.ai.TextWave` | text clips | `amplitude`, `speed`, `wavelength` |

### ColorLut

`tellers.ai.ColorLut`: a `.cube` LUT graded on a clip, a track or the whole timeline. Like the effects above, its data is in `parameters`:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `asset_id` | string: the `.cube` asset, what the timeline stores |
| `cube_url` | string: the URL the player downloads, resolved from `asset_id` before playback and stripped before saving |

Both used to be written beside `parameters`, directly in `tellers.ai`; they are still read there, and `sanitize` moves them in.

### Animatable parameters

A numeric parameter is either a plain number or keyframes:

```json
{ "keyframes": [ { "t": 0, "v": 0, "ease": "easeOut" }, { "t": 1.5, "v": 8 } ] }
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `t` | Seconds from the start of the clip on the timeline (not source time). |
| `v` | The value at `t`. |
| `ease` | The curve from this keyframe to the next. |

Before the first keyframe the value is the first one's, after the last the last one's. Keyframes are read sorted by `t`.

| `ease` | Curve |
|---|---|
| `linear` | straight line (the default) |
| `hold` | keeps this keyframe's value until the next keyframe |
| `easeIn` | starts slow: `x³` |
| `easeOut` | ends slow: `1 − (1 − x)³` |
| `easeInOut` | slow at both ends (cubic) |
